Title: Persist every grade change to a rating history table
Description:
As the credit desk supervisor I want every grade change written to a history table so that I can answer an audit question about who changed what without restoring a backup.

Constraints, all of which come from live dependencies:
- The response shape of POST /api/ratings/{issuerId}/grade is frozen. A 2019 desktop client reads the four values out of that object positionally and breaks if a key is added, removed or reordered. RatingsApiTest.updateGradeResponseShapeIsFrozen is the contract.
- There is no migration tool in this service. Schema changes go into ratings-service/src/main/resources/schema.sql, which the desk DBA applies by hand against staging and production, so the file has to stay idempotent.
- The existing tests stay green. Do not edit them.
- A grade change that succeeds but fails to write history is a defect. A history write must not leave the ratings row updated on its own.
Acceptance Criteria:
- A rating_history row is written for every successful grade change, capturing issuer, previous grade, new grade, previous outlook, new outlook, the caller and a timestamp.
- schema.sql creates the table with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and can be run twice.
- POST /api/ratings/{issuerId}/grade returns exactly the same JSON as before, key for key and in the same order.
- A failed history write rolls the grade change back.
- New tests cover the history row contents and the rollback.

Title: Expose the grade history for an issuer
Description:
As a credit analyst I want GET /api/ratings/{issuerId}/history so that I can see how an issuer's grade moved without asking the data team for a query.

Depends on the rating history table from the previous story. Newest change first. The endpoint is read only and lives on the public API surface, not under /api/admin.
Acceptance Criteria:
- GET /api/ratings/{issuerId}/history returns the change history newest first.
- An issuer that does not exist returns 404.
- An issuer that exists but has never been regraded returns 200 with an empty array, not 404.
- Tests cover the not-found case and the empty-history case.

Title: Filter the ratings search by sector
Description:
As a credit analyst I want to narrow a ratings search to one sector so that a search for a common word does not return the whole book.

The sector parameter already exists on GET /api/ratings/search. It is undocumented and untested, and the sector list is not validated against anything.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The sector values accepted by the endpoint are validated against the sectors present in the ratings table.
- An unknown sector returns 400 with a message naming the valid values.
- Tests cover a valid sector, an unknown sector and no sector.

Title: Retire the h2-console from the deployed service
Description:
As the platform owner I want the H2 console disabled outside local development so that the deployed service does not expose a database shell.

spring.h2.console.enabled is true in application.yml and there is no profile separation in this service yet.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The H2 console is disabled by default and enabled only under a local profile.
- Actuator exposure is reduced to health and info by default.
- The service still starts locally with the console available.

Title: Record export jobs in the export_jobs table
Description:
As the batch team I want each export run recorded in the export_jobs table that already exists in schema.sql so that a failed overnight run can be traced without reading container logs.

The table is created but nothing writes to it.
Acceptance Criteria:
- POST /api/exports/run inserts a job row with a generated id, the format, the desk, the start time and a state.
- The state moves to COMPLETED or FAILED when the run finishes.
- A test covers both outcomes.

Title: Publish an OpenAPI description of the public API
Description:
As a consumer of the ratings API I want a machine readable description of the endpoints so that I can generate a client instead of reading the controllers.

The frozen response shape of the grade update has to be described exactly as it is, including key order, with the reason stated in the description.
Acceptance Criteria:
- An OpenAPI 3 document is served and covers every endpoint under /api/ratings and /api/exports.
- The grade update response is documented as a frozen contract.
- The build fails if the document cannot be generated.

Title: Feed ingestion accepts a document with no issuers and reports success
Description: POST /api/feed/xml returns 200 and an empty array when the overnight feed arrives empty or with a changed root element. The overnight job treats that as a successful ingest and the desk finds out a day later that no ratings moved.
Acceptance Criteria:
- An XML document containing no issuer elements is rejected with 400.
- The error names the root element that was found.
- A test covers the empty feed and a feed with a changed root element.

Title: Grade update accepts any string as a grade
Description: POST /api/ratings/{issuerId}/grade writes whatever string it is given. A typo in the desktop client put 'AAA-' into the book in January and nothing rejected it.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Grades are validated against the set of grades the desk uses.
- An invalid grade returns 400 and does not change the row.
- The response shape for a successful update is unchanged.
